outcome: The Oracle Reconciliation phase closes only when end-to-end connectivity and architecture alignment are both proven: logical Oracle infrastructure ownership matches physical module/dependency ownership, current concrete context flows still work, external/internal source seams are reachable, and closure machinery detects future architecture-to-source placement drift.
currentProblem: The prior Oracle-detail closure declared zero debt because it checked generic-abstraction pressure rather than logical-to-physical architecture alignment. Without a phase-level acceptance task and a durable closure invariant, the same debt can recur even after moving files.
constraints: Phase acceptance consumes delivered outputs from BB-060 through BB-063; it cannot replace them with one monolithic refactor.
Declared logical ownership and physical package/dependency ownership must be mechanically or deterministically checkable.
Acceptance must exercise real Backend repository-context and QA accepted-artifact context paths through the extracted Oracle boundary.
Architecture checks must detect Oracle implementation leaking back into Agentic Application/Core packages.
Closure must not require a generic Resolver framework, third source class, MCP deployment or unrelated feature work.
successCriteria: Phase acceptance proves current Backend and QA flows cross the infrastructure-owned Oracle boundary end to end.
A deterministic architecture check fails when Oracle implementation is placed back under Agentic Application/Core ownership or dependency direction reverses.
Repository and application-artifact connectivity preserve exact source/provenance semantics after extraction.
All BB-060..063 obligations are represented by durable delivered evidence before the topic can be considered closed.
Living Oracle architecture/state and physical source topology converge on the same ownership model with no known reconciliation debt.
